title: Gov. Hochul, Bruce Blakeman make closing arguments before Election Day - ABC7 New York
text:
Gov. Hochul, Bruce Blakeman make closing arguments before Election Day | abc7ny.com 
 Politics Hochul, Blakeman make closing arguments before Election Day
 WABC By Phil Taitt Updated 1 hour ago Phil Taitt reported live from Harlem. HARLEM, New York City (WABC) -- With Election Day approaching, Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman spent Monday making their final appeals to voters as early voting totals topped 690,000 ballots statewide.[br /][br /]According to state early voting figures, more than 690,000 voters had already cast ballots in New York City ahead of Election Day. Brooklyn led all boroughs with 219,536 early votes, followed by Manhattan. Democrats have outpaced Republicans during the early voting period, though Republicans historically are more likely to vote on Election Day.[br /][br /][media ID="20007498" /][br /][br /]Hochul, who is seeking a second full term as governor, was scheduled to campaign Monday morning at a Harlem subway station as she continued efforts to boost turnout in key Democratic strongholds. The governor spent Sunday in Astoria alongside Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.[br /][br /]Blakeman, the Nassau County executive, campaigned Sunday in Northport with Rep. Nick LaLota and Suffolk County Executive Ed Romaine. On Monday, he planned a statewide campaign tour beginning in Bethpage, with stops in Buffalo, Rochester, Syracuse and Binghamton before ending the day in Manhattan.[br /][br /]As the race entered its final hours, both candidates continued to criticize one another.[br /][br /][b]MORE: [url HREF="https://abc7ny.com/vote2026/" TARGET="" REL=""]Vote 2026[/url] [/b][br /][br /]"Kathy Hochul and Zohran Mamdani have a pact now, a secret pact. We know about it. To raise taxes. Mamdani has talked about raising taxes. Kathy Hochul won't rule it out," Blakeman said.[br /][br /]Hochul emphasized cooperation between state and city leaders.[br /][br /]"It's important that we team up the state and the city for the betterment of New York City residents... I have the ball in my hand— running toward the end zone but we're not there yet."[br /][br /]While campaign events continued Monday, there was no early voting.
